hits.full_text: Underrated life advice: Always default to praise of people who aren’t in the room. The way you talk about someone who’s not in the room is a loud signal about the energy you carry. Say something kind. Specific. Or nothing at all. Negativity does more harm to you than anyone else.
hits.hook: SahilBloom: default to praise of people who aren't in the room; kind, specific, or nothing (best brand fit today)
hits.draft_en:
I've started noticing what I say about people after they leave the room.

It tells me more about my week than about them.

On a good day it's something kind and specific. On a rough day, the best I can do is say nothing.
hits.video_tip: 10 seconds, no face. Two coffee cups on a wooden table, one chair pushed back as if someone just left. A hand writes one kind line on an index card and tucks it under the empty cup. Room sound only. Last frame text: 'Kind and specific.'

hits.name: Dan Koe
hits.media_note: text-only; open replies; combative edge ('victim card'), soften before using
hits.text: Most people who say they don't care about money spend their entire lives controlled by it. They feel noble for not trying to improve their financial situation,…
hits.full_text:
Most people who say they don't care about money spend their entire lives controlled by it. They feel noble for not trying to improve their financial situation, but when the bills pile up and they can't take advantage of any (most) opportunities that require money, they pull the victim card.

It's okay. You can say it. Money is important. That doesn't make you a bad person.
hits.hook: thedankoe: people who say they don't care about money are controlled by it; money is important (soften: knowing the number)
hits.draft_en:
Not caring about money and not looking at money are two different things.

A lot of us do the second one and call it the first.

Knowing the actual number is quieter than guessing at it.
hits.video_tip: 12 seconds, overhead, no face, no real figures shown. A hand writes a column of numbers in ink, the camera stays soft-focused so nothing is legible, then the pen underlines the total. Room sound only. Last frame text: 'Knowing is quieter.'

reply_ideas.reply_text: The word I'd underline is specific. "She's great" costs nothing. Naming the exact thing someone did well shows you were paying attention, and that's the part that gets back to them.
Caring about money and being run by it are different things. The people who seem calmest about it aren't the ones pretending it doesn't matter. They're the ones who know their actual numbers.
What stays with me in so many sobriety stories is how small the promise gets. Not forever, just today. Curious what Rich said helped on the days when even today felt too big.

Two thousand saves says a lot of people needed a reset this week. For me a reset has to be small enough to start today, or it turns into another plan. Curious which piece of this people actually kept.
